extraction.Name: William Bridgeman
extraction.Refused/Protested: Yes I told the man that gave it to me that I did not want it and had not asked for it and he said that it had been issued and it would be necessary for me to take it.
extraction.Buyer: First mortgaged for $1500.00; then Joseph Keller and Frank Krein (known as Brownie Krein) made arrangements to purchase the land for consideration of paying off the mortgage of $1500.00, pay the taxes of $800.00, and pay $650.00 in cash; deed conveyed in favor of Winnie M. Keller for one dollar and other valuable consideration on November 21, 1923
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: pay the taxes of $850 $800.00 was part of the purchase consideration
extraction.NOTES: Allottee received a Haynes car valued at $1000.00 and $500 in cash as part of an arrangement made by Clement Whirlwing Soldier, T. C. Montgomery, and another man from Winner. Allottee states he first signed what he believed was a mortgage for $1500.00, not a deed. When away from home, signed papers after receiving $200.00, not knowing it was a deed. Agreed to wait until mid-November for remainder of money ($425.00 still unpaid). Deed was signed but allottee states he did not deliver it. James Andrews and one of James's boys were also present and aware of the deal. Allottee went to see purchasers 3 times after but got no satisfaction.
